title: What to eat
intro: Osaka's food identity is takoyaki, okonomiyaki and kushikatsu — the crawl below sticks to those rather than padding in a ramen stop; reviews on Osaka's famous ramen chains (Kinryu, Ichiran) run mixed, and neither is a specifically Osaka dish. Kani Doraku's giant crab sign is a photo stop, not a booking — ¥5,000–10,000/person for reviews that call the ingredients hit-or-miss. Two independent resident food bloggers make the same point about Dotonbori's biggest-signage shops generally: the flashier the storefront, the more it's priced for tourists and queued accordingly — Kouga-ryu below is one of their tested alternatives.

items.name: Mizuno
items.how: 2 min walk from Namba Station exit B22
items.crowd_tip: Walk-in only — queues daily, worse on weekends. Arrive at open or budget a 30–60 min wait.
items.why: Michelin Bib Gourmand okonomiyaki with a yamaimo (mountain yam) batter — natural umami instead of the usual thick-sauce version.

items.name: Kushikatsu Daruma
items.hours: 11:00–22:30 weekdays, 10:30–22:30 weekends (last order 30 min before close)
items.how: In the Dotonbori arcade, a few minutes' walk from Namba Station
items.crowd_tip: Reservable weekdays 11am–6pm for parties of 2+; call ahead or use the site. Evenings and weekends are walk-in and can queue.
items.why: The standard-bearer kushikatsu chain — the 'no double-dipping the shared sauce' rule is half the fun. The original 1929 Shinsekai flagship is further out (Naniwa-ku), walk-in only, worth it as a separate pilgrimage rather than a swap for this stop.

items.name: Wanaka
items.how: In the Dotonbori arcade, a short walk from Namba Station
items.crowd_tip: ⚠ Address/hours above are aggregator-corroborated only — the official site returned a certificate error on the attempted fetch. Confirm before relying on them. A Kuromon Ichiba branch exists too — worth a stop there instead if visiting the market anyway, best before 11am to dodge the lines that build by midday.
items.why: Crispy-outside, fluffy-inside takoyaki — order 'half & half' to try two sauce styles at once.

items.name: Kouga-ryu
items.hours: 10:30–20:30 daily (10:30–21:30 Saturdays and the day before public holidays)
items.how: In Amerikamura, a short walk from the Dotonbori strip — not on the canal-front tourist row itself
items.crowd_tip: A resident food blogger names this her tested alternative to the queued, tourist-priced takoyaki shops fronting the Dotonbori canal.
items.why: Takoyaki a few minutes off the main strip, at local prices without the wait.

items.name: Abaraya
items.how: A block off the Namba tourist strip, in Sennichimae
items.crowd_tip: Genuinely local clientele despite sitting a block from the Namba tourist strip. No English menu — point-and-order is normal here.
items.why: Battera (pressed, vinegared mackerel sushi) — Osaka's own sushi style, easy to miss next to the takoyaki/okonomiyaki circuit.

items.name: Houshoan
items.how: In the Pontocho alley, walking distance from Kawaramachi or Gion-Shijo Station
items.crowd_tip: Book via the site's online form. Booking window, cancellation policy and foreign-card acceptance aren't stated on the page — a follow-up call is worth it before counting on the reservation.
items.why: Kaiseki or wagyu-sukiyaki in a Pontocho alley — the reservation-depth pick for the trip's one dedicated splurge dinner.

items.name: Nakamura Tokichi Honten
items.area: Uji, Kyoto (day-trip detour from central Kyoto)
items.how: 2 min walk from JR Uji Station — a ~20 min JR Nara Line ride from Kyoto Station, not on this itinerary's main loop
items.crowd_tip: Walk-in only for regular café seating (numbered tickets from 10am) — real waits are normal; a reservation-only weekend 'zashiki' room exists separately.
items.why: Matcha specialist since 1854, 7th generation — a detour worth it only if a Uji side-trip is already on the table; skip if the itinerary stays inside Osaka/Kyoto/Nara proper.

items.name: Kakinohazushi Tanaka
items.address: 5-2 Higashimuki-nakamachi, Nara — 2 min from Kintetsu Nara Station
items.how: 2 min walk from Kintetsu Nara Station
items.why: Kakinoha-zushi (persimmon-leaf-wrapped sushi), a Nara specialty since 1903 — has an in-store tea room for eating in rather than taking away.
